Redwoods, the Russian River and one steep climb

Getting around. The rules.

Guerneville is a small Sonoma County town on the Russian River, with redwoods north and the coast west. One loop starts in town: 26 miles over Sweetwater Springs Road, with a 2.3-mile climb at 8.8 percent. We found no bike shop in town; the nearest is in Forestville, about 6 miles east in a straight line. Cycle to Zero, San Francisco AIDS Foundation’s three-day ride, is May 21–23, 2027. Riders camp here two nights, Friday and Saturday, May 21 and 22.

Best months
Summer is when the river town is fully open. Johnson’s Beach gives two seasons on its own pages: Memorial Day to October 1 on one, and on its FAQ a 2026 season of daily from June 1 through September 7. The farmers market is listed for June through August. The Russian River floods in winter, so check the roads after storms.
Nearest airport
Charles M. Schulz–Sonoma County Airport (STS), 10 mi
Major airport
San Francisco International (SFO), 70 mi

Clubs and collectives in Guerneville

  1. Santa Rosa Cycling Club

    The county’s big road club, and the one whose calendar reaches the river. Rides most days at 9:30 am from parks in Sebastopol, Windsor, Healdsburg and Santa Rosa, and some from Monte Rio and Graton. In November 2026 its calendar had a ride from Sebastopol to Guerneville and two coast rides from the Monte Rio Community Center. Each listing gives a terrain number, a pace letter and the miles. A non-member can ride once after signing the waiver at the start; after that you join ($25 a year, or a free 90-day trial, read Nov 2026). The King Ridge and Sonoma Coast routes in this guide are the club’s.

  2. Sports Basement Santa Rosa

    No-drop

    A shop that leads a free road ride from inside the store at 1970 Santa Rosa Ave. Most routes are 30 to 40 miles and nobody is left behind. Show up; the shop posts changes on its Strava club. Day and time: the shop’s no-drop ride (Last Sunday of the month, 9:00 am). It’s in Santa Rosa, about 16 miles southeast of Guerneville in a straight line.

    In the directory: Last Sunday Ride (Last Sunday of the month, 9:00 am) →

  3. Santa Rosa Taco Tuesday Ride

    A community evening ride through central Santa Rosa to the taco trucks at Mitote Food Park and back, 8 miles round trip, all year. Free, show up. Rain and holidays cancel it. Worth it if you’re already in Santa Rosa on a Tuesday; not a reason to drive from the river.

How Guerneville rides: the zones, getting here

About Guerneville

Guerneville sits on State Route 116 along the Russian River in Sonoma County, at 59 feet. It had 4,552 people at the 2020 census. It isn’t a city. It’s an unincorporated community, so there’s no city hall. This guide covers the town and the lower river around it. Upriver, that’s Rio Nido and Korbel. Just downriver, Guernewood Park and Vacation Beach. Toward the coast, Monte Rio and Duncans Mills. Forestville is to the east. Sebastopol and Santa Rosa are different towns. They’re here only for the bike shops and the group rides, because Guerneville has neither.

It’s written for two readers. The first is the Cycle to Zero rider. The ride is May 21–23, 2027. Riders camp both nights, Friday and Saturday, at Camp Russian River and Johnson’s Beach, about a 15-minute walk apart. Day 2 is about 40 miles or about 100 miles from Guerneville, or a day off the bike. That’s the day for coffee and a walk in the redwoods. The second reader is whoever drives up to meet a rider and needs a room. Or anyone who comes to the river with a bike on another weekend.

Know three things before you come. We found no bike shop in town. The nearest is Russian River Cycle Service in Forestville, and it’s closed Sunday to Tuesday. One coffee place opens at 6 every day, Coffee Bazaar. Several places to stay are adults only by their own rules. Read the hotel notes before you book for a family. We found no club or weekly group ride that starts in Guerneville. The Santa Rosa Cycling Club starts some rides in Monte Rio and Sebastopol.

Riding in Guerneville

Start with the loop from town. The Sweetwater Springs Road loop is 26 miles and about 2,300 feet. It goes north on Armstrong Woods Road, nearly flat, then turns onto Sweetwater Springs Road. The climb is 2.3 miles at 8.8 percent, with short pitches of 16 percent or more. It comes home on Westside Road and River Road past Korbel and Rio Nido. River Road has heavy traffic.

The long days start downriver. King Ridge is 55 miles from Monte Rio. It goes up Austin Creek to Cazadero, along the ridge and down to Highway 1. It comes back through Jenner and Duncans Mills. The Santa Rosa Cycling Club calls it very remote. It counts two water stops in the 40 miles to Jenner. The club’s Sonoma Coast loop is 34 miles from Occidental. It passes through Monte Rio, so you can join it there.

The easy one is a drive away. The West County Regional Trail is a county rail-trail, 5.5 miles each way from Forestville through Graton to Sebastopol. It does not reach Guerneville, and no published path links the two. The county’s parks department says the river corridor has too few sidewalks and bike lanes and no shared paths. A separate river trail is still a proposal.

The 5 routes, with maps →

Getting to Guerneville

Drive. Guerneville has no airport and no train. It’s on State Route 116 along the Russian River. Sonoma County Airport (STS) in Santa Rosa is the close one, about 10 miles east in a straight line. The drive is longer. Alaska, American, Southwest and Delta fly there. Nine rental car brands have counters in baggage claim (the airport’s own pages, 2026). San Francisco International is about 70 miles southeast in a straight line, and Oakland about 69. Groome Transportation runs buses from both to the STS stop, about 2.25 to 2.5 hours, from $39 one way from SFO (Nov 2026). Its FAQ says bikes ride at no extra charge. That gets you to Santa Rosa, not to the river. Without a car, there’s Sonoma County Transit’s Route 20. It runs between Santa Rosa and Monte Rio through Sebastopol, Forestville, Rio Nido and Guerneville. Every bus has a bike rack. It’s a thin schedule. The last bus toward the river that runs every day leaves Coddingtown at 5:20 pm (timetable effective April 12, 2026). The SMART train comes no closer than Santa Rosa.

Questions about cycling in Guerneville

Which Guerneville hotels lend bikes to guests?

Three say so on their own pages. boon hotel + spa says “We have cruiser bikes available complimentary to our guests,” Dawn Ranch offers its “complimentary fleet of Retrospec bikes,” and The Stavrand says “Take out one of our cheerful yellow bicycles for a spin (first-come, first-served).” None of them states a policy on bringing your own bike into the room, so ask when you book.

What coffee shop in Guerneville opens at 6 a.m.?

Coffee Bazaar, downtown at 14045 Armstrong Woods Rd, opens at 6 a.m. every day, Saturday and Sunday included. The Farmhand on River Road opens at 9 and is closed Tuesday and Wednesday, so it’s for after the ride.

Is there a bike shop in Guerneville, and where is the nearest one?

We found no bike shop in Guerneville. The nearest is Russian River Cycle Service at 6559 Front St. in Forestville, about 6 miles east in a straight line, open Wednesday to Friday 11 to 6 and Saturday 9 to 5 and closed Sunday to Tuesday. Revel Cycles in Sebastopol, about 12 miles southeast in a straight line, is open every day 11 to 6.

Where can I rent a bike near the Russian River?

We found nothing to rent in Guerneville itself. Russian River Cycle Service in Forestville, about 6 miles east in a straight line, rents road bikes for $75 a day and hybrids for $45, by appointment seven days a week (Nov 2026). Sports Basement in Santa Rosa has the widest range, with carbon road bikes at $100 a day (chain rates, Nov 2026), and Revel Cycles in Sebastopol rents e-bikes and cruisers only.

What bike routes start in or near Guerneville?

One loop starts in town: the Sweetwater Springs Road loop, 26 miles and about 2,300 feet, with a climb of 2.3 miles at 8.8%. King Ridge, 55 miles, starts in Monte Rio, and the Sonoma Coast loop, 34 miles, starts in Occidental and passes through Monte Rio. The car-free path is the West County Regional Trail, 5.5 miles each way from Forestville to Sebastopol; it does not reach Guerneville.

Where do Cycle to Zero riders sleep in Guerneville?

They camp. Cycle to Zero is May 21–23, 2027, and riders camp two nights, Friday and Saturday, May 21 and 22, at Camp Russian River and Johnson’s Beach, about a 15-minute walk apart. The hotels in this guide are for whoever drives up to meet a rider.
